ABT: Abbott Laboratories is a global healthcare company that discovers, develops, manufactures, and sells a broad range of health care products. The company operates through four segments: Established Pharmaceutical Products, Diagnostic Products, Nutritional Products, and Medical Devices. Abbott is known for its FreeStyle Libre continuous glucose monitoring system, a market-leading diabetes care product, as well as its diagnostics business which expanded significantly during COVID-19. The company has a long history of consistent dividend growth, making it a Dividend Aristocrat.
A: Agilent Technologies is a global leader in life sciences, diagnostics, and applied chemical markets. The company provides instruments, software, services, and consumables for laboratories worldwide. Agilent's products are used in pharmaceutical and biotech research, clinical diagnostics, food safety testing, and environmental analysis. Spun off from Hewlett-Packard in 1999, the company has grown into one of the most important analytical instrument makers in the world.
ADI: Analog Devices is a global semiconductor company specializing in data conversion, signal conditioning, and power management technology. The company designs, manufactures, and markets analog, mixed-signal, and digital signal processing integrated circuits used in virtually all types of electronic equipment. ADI serves customers across industrial, automotive, communications, and consumer end markets. Its 2021 acquisition of Maxim Integrated significantly expanded its product portfolio and market reach.
ATO: Atmos Energy Corporation is one of the largest natural gas distribution companies in the United States, delivering natural gas to over three million customers in eight states. The company operates through two segments: Distribution and Pipeline and Storage. Atmos Energy has a strong track record of capital investment in pipeline safety and reliability, and is recognized as one of the most consistently growing utilities in the country with a long history of dividend increases.
ADP: Automatic Data Processing is one of the largest providers of human capital management solutions worldwide. The company offers cloud-based payroll processing, human resources management, talent management, tax and benefits administration, and compliance services. ADP serves approximately 1 million clients globally, ranging from small businesses to large enterprises, and processes payroll for roughly one in six U.S. workers. The company is a Dividend Aristocrat with over 40 consecutive years of dividend increases.
BKH: Black Hills Corporation is a diversified energy company serving 1.3 million natural gas and electric utility customers across eight states in the western United States. The company operates through its Electric Utilities and Gas Utilities segments, providing regulated electric and natural gas service. Black Hills has a long history of dividend growth, having increased its dividend for over 50 consecutive years, making it one of the longest streaks among U.S. utilities.
CAT: Caterpillar Inc. is the world's leading manufacturer of construction and mining equipment, diesel and natural gas engines, industrial gas turbines, and diesel-electric locomotives. The company operates through three primary segments: Construction Industries, Resource Industries, and Energy & Transportation. Caterpillar products are sold in nearly every country, and the company is widely considered a bellwether for global economic activity. CAT is a Dividend Aristocrat with over 25 consecutive years of dividend increases.
CHD: Church & Dwight Co. is a leading consumer packaged goods company that manufactures and markets a broad range of household, personal care, and specialty products. The company's portfolio includes well-known brands such as Arm & Hammer, OxiClean, Trojan, First Response, Batiste, and Waterpik. Church & Dwight has consistently delivered above-average organic growth in the consumer staples sector and maintains a strong record of dividend increases.
CL: Colgate-Palmolive Company is a global consumer products company focused on oral care, personal care, home care, and pet nutrition. The company's products are sold in over 200 countries under brands including Colgate, Palmolive, Ajax, Hill's Science Diet, and Tom's of Maine. Colgate holds the #1 global market share in toothpaste and is one of the most recognized consumer brands worldwide. The company has paid uninterrupted dividends since 1895.
FAST: Fastenal Company is a leading distributor of industrial and construction supplies in North America. The company operates through a network of approximately 1,700 branch locations and over 1,800 Onsite locations embedded within customer facilities. Fastenal distributes fasteners, safety products, cutting tools, hydraulics, and other industrial supplies. The company's unique vending machine program and Onsite model have driven consistent growth and market share gains in the industrial distribution space.
GD: General Dynamics Corporation is a global aerospace and defense company that offers a broad portfolio of products and services in business aviation, ship construction and repair, land combat vehicles, weapons systems, and technology solutions. The company operates through four segments: Aerospace (Gulfstream jets), Marine Systems (submarines, surface ships), Combat Systems (armored vehicles), and Technologies. General Dynamics is one of the top five U.S. defense contractors by revenue.
GPC: Genuine Parts Company is a leading distributor of automotive and industrial replacement parts. The company operates through its Automotive Parts Group, which includes the NAPA Auto Parts brand in North America, and its Industrial Parts Group, which distributes industrial replacement parts. GPC has operations across North America, Europe, and Australasia. The company is a Dividend King, having increased its dividend for over 65 consecutive years.
LRCX: Lam Research Corporation is one of the world's leading suppliers of semiconductor manufacturing equipment. The company designs, manufactures, and services wafer fabrication equipment used in the production of integrated circuits. Lam's products are essential for etching, deposition, and cleaning processes in chip manufacturing. The company holds dominant market share in plasma etch and has been a key beneficiary of increasing chip complexity and the global semiconductor buildout.
LMT: Lockheed Martin Corporation is the world's largest defense contractor, specializing in aerospace, defense, arms, security, and advanced technologies. The company operates through four business segments: Aeronautics (including the F-35 fighter jet), Missiles and Fire Control, Rotary and Mission Systems, and Space. Lockheed Martin is a primary contractor for the U.S. Department of Defense and numerous allied nations, and generates the majority of its revenue from government contracts.
MATX: Matson, Inc. is a leading provider of ocean transportation and logistics services in the Pacific. The company operates a fleet of vessels providing containership service to Hawaii, Alaska, Guam, Micronesia, and select South Pacific island economies, as well as a premium expedited service from China to Southern California. Matson also operates a logistics business providing multimodal transportation, warehousing, and distribution services across North America.
NEE: NextEra Energy is the world's largest generator of renewable energy from wind and solar, and one of the largest electric utilities in the United States. The company operates through Florida Power & Light (FPL), the largest rate-regulated electric utility in the country, and NextEra Energy Resources, the world's largest generator of renewable energy from wind and solar. NEE has delivered consistent earnings growth and is widely regarded as the premier utility growth stock.
ORI: Old Republic International Corporation is a diversified insurance holding company that focuses on commercial lines of insurance. The company operates through three segments: General Insurance, Title Insurance, and the Republic Financial Indemnity Group run-off business. Old Republic has a long track record of profitability and has paid uninterrupted dividends for over 80 years, making it one of the longest dividend streaks of any U.S. company.
PCAR: PACCAR Inc is a global technology leader in the design, manufacture, and support of premium light-, medium-, and heavy-duty trucks under the Kenworth, Peterbilt, and DAF nameplates. The company also provides financial services, information technology, and distributes truck parts through its PACCAR Parts division. PACCAR is known for its premium quality products, strong balance sheet, and consistent profitability throughout economic cycles.
QCOM: Qualcomm Incorporated is a global leader in wireless technology and semiconductor design. The company develops and licenses wireless technology and designs and sells semiconductor products used in mobile devices, automotive, IoT, and computing. Qualcomm's Snapdragon processors power the majority of premium Android smartphones worldwide, and the company holds an extensive patent portfolio covering fundamental wireless communications technologies including 5G, 4G, and Wi-Fi.
DGX: Quest Diagnostics is the largest provider of diagnostic information services in the United States. The company offers a broad range of clinical laboratory testing services used by physicians, hospitals, managed care organizations, employers, and government agencies. Quest processes approximately 200 million test requisitions annually through its network of laboratories and patient service centers, making it a critical part of the U.S. healthcare infrastructure.
SSNC: SS&C Technologies Holdings is one of the largest global providers of financial technology software and services for the financial services and healthcare industries. The company offers cloud-based solutions for fund administration, portfolio management, accounting, risk and compliance, and healthcare data management. SS&C serves approximately 20,000 clients in the financial services industry, including hedge funds, asset managers, banks, and insurance companies.
STLD: Steel Dynamics is one of the largest domestic steel producers and metals recyclers in the United States. The company operates through three segments: Steel Operations, Metals Recycling, and Steel Fabrication. Steel Dynamics is recognized as an industry leader in operating efficiency and financial performance, utilizing electric arc furnace steelmaking technology. The company has consistently invested in growth and diversification while maintaining strong free cash flow generation.
SYK: Stryker Corporation is one of the world's leading medical technology companies. The company offers a diverse array of innovative medical products and services in orthopedics, medical and surgical, and neurotechnology and spine. Stryker's products include joint replacement implants, surgical equipment, neurovascular devices, and emergency medical equipment. The company has a strong track record of consistent growth through both organic innovation and strategic acquisitions.
TEL: TE Connectivity is a global industrial technology company and one of the world's largest manufacturers of connectors and sensors. The company designs and manufactures products that connect and protect the flow of power, data, and signal in a wide range of applications across transportation, industrial, and communications end markets. TE's products are essential components in automotive, aerospace, industrial equipment, and data communications infrastructure.
VLO: Valero Energy Corporation is the world's largest independent petroleum refiner and a major renewable fuels producer. The company operates 15 petroleum refineries with a combined throughput capacity of approximately 3.2 million barrels per day. Valero also operates 12 ethanol plants and a renewable diesel plant. The company is a leading producer of renewable diesel and sustainable aviation fuel, positioning it at the intersection of traditional energy and the energy transition.
AMD: Advanced Micro Devices is a global semiconductor company designing and selling high-performance computing, graphics, and visualization technologies. AMD's product portfolio includes Ryzen processors for PCs, EPYC processors for data centers, Radeon graphics cards, and Instinct accelerators for AI and machine learning workloads. The company's 2022 acquisition of Xilinx expanded its capabilities into adaptive computing. AMD has gained significant market share from Intel in both the PC and server markets.
AEM: Agnico Eagle Mines is one of the world's largest gold mining companies, with operations in Canada, Australia, Finland, and Mexico. The company has a strong track record of operational performance and financial discipline, consistently delivering robust gold production from its portfolio of high-quality, long-life mines. Agnico Eagle is known for its low-risk geographic profile, strong balance sheet, and commitment to responsible mining practices.
ATAT: Atour Lifestyle Holdings is a leading hotel group in China focused on the upper-midscale to midscale hotel segments. The company operates primarily under the Atour brand and manages a rapidly growing portfolio of hotels across major Chinese cities. Atour differentiates itself through its lifestyle-oriented approach, offering curated in-room amenities and retail products. The company has demonstrated strong unit growth and improving profitability as it scales its asset-light franchise model.
CVX: Chevron Corporation is one of the world's largest integrated energy companies, with operations spanning oil and gas exploration and production, refining, chemicals, and renewable energy. The company operates in virtually every segment of the energy industry and has significant assets in the Permian Basin, offshore Gulf of Mexico, and international locations including Australia and Kazakhstan. Chevron has increased its dividend for over 35 consecutive years and maintains one of the strongest balance sheets among the oil majors.
CWAN: Clearwater Analytics Holdings is a leading provider of SaaS-based investment accounting, reporting, and analytics solutions. The company's cloud-native platform automates the entire investment lifecycle for insurance companies, asset managers, corporations, and government entities. Clearwater aggregates data from over 1,800 custodians and data sources, providing a single source of truth for investment portfolios. The company has demonstrated strong recurring revenue growth since its founding in 2004.
CNX: CNX Resources Corporation is a leading Appalachian Basin natural gas producer focused on developing its substantial resource base in the Marcellus and Utica shale formations. The company is recognized for its low-cost production structure, strong free cash flow generation, and innovative approach to emissions reduction. CNX has been a pioneer in responsibly sourced natural gas and has committed to significant emissions reduction targets across its operations.
COIN: Coinbase Global is the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the United States and one of the largest globally by trading volume. The company provides a trusted platform for buying, selling, transferring, and storing digital assets for retail users, institutional investors, and developers. Coinbase generates revenue primarily from transaction fees, subscription and services revenue, and custodial services. The company went public via direct listing in April 2021.
EIX: Edison International is one of the largest electric utilities in the United States, serving approximately 5 million customers through its subsidiary Southern California Edison. The company provides electricity across a 50,000-square-mile service territory in central, coastal, and Southern California. Edison International is a leader in renewable energy procurement and grid modernization, with one of the cleanest generation portfolios among major U.S. utilities.
FINV: FinVolution Group is a leading fintech platform connecting underserved borrowers with financial institutions in China and internationally. The company uses proprietary AI and big data analytics to facilitate consumer lending, providing credit assessment and loan facilitation services. FinVolution has expanded beyond China into Indonesia, the Philippines, and other Southeast Asian markets, diversifying its revenue base and reducing country-specific risk.
FTNT: Fortinet is a global leader in cybersecurity, providing broad, integrated, and automated security solutions. The company's flagship FortiGate next-generation firewall platform is the most widely deployed network firewall in the world. Fortinet's Security Fabric architecture provides end-to-end protection across the entire digital attack surface, from network and cloud to endpoints and IoT. The company has consistently gained market share in the cybersecurity industry.
GFI: Gold Fields Limited is a globally diversified gold producer with operations in South Africa, Ghana, Australia, and Peru, and a project in Chile. The company is one of the world's largest gold mining companies by production volume. Gold Fields has been focused on extending mine life, improving operational efficiency, and developing its pipeline of growth projects. The company offers investors exposure to gold prices through a portfolio of high-quality, long-life mining assets.
SUPV: Grupo Supervielle is a leading financial services group in Argentina, providing banking, insurance, consumer finance, and asset management services. The company operates through Banco Supervielle, one of the largest private banks in Argentina, serving individuals, small and medium enterprises, and large corporations. Supervielle has been expanding its digital banking capabilities and fintech offerings to capture growth in Argentina's underbanked population.
HRMY: Harmony Biosciences Holdings is a commercial-stage pharmaceutical company focused on developing and commercializing therapies for patients with rare neurological diseases. The company's lead product, WAKIX (pitolisant), is the first and only FDA-approved treatment for excessive daytime sleepiness in adults with narcolepsy that works through a novel mechanism of action on histamine H3 receptors. Harmony has been expanding WAKIX's label and exploring additional indications.
HUT: Hut 8 Corp. is one of North America's largest Bitcoin mining companies, operating a fleet of mining facilities powered primarily by renewable and carbon-free energy sources. Following its merger with US Bitcoin Corp in 2023, the company expanded its operations significantly and diversified into high-performance computing and AI infrastructure services. Hut 8 holds one of the largest self-mined Bitcoin reserves of any publicly traded company.
KEYS: Keysight Technologies is a leading technology company that delivers advanced design, test, and measurement solutions. The company helps enterprises, service providers, and governments accelerate innovation in 5G, autonomous vehicles, IoT, and cybersecurity. Spun off from Agilent Technologies in 2014, Keysight has grown into the world's largest electronic test and measurement company, serving customers in communications, aerospace, defense, automotive, and semiconductor industries.
MARA: MARA Holdings (formerly Marathon Digital Holdings) is one of the largest Bitcoin mining companies in the world by hash rate. The company operates large-scale Bitcoin mining facilities across the United States and internationally, utilizing a mix of energy sources with an increasing focus on renewable energy. MARA has been actively expanding its mining capacity and diversifying its operations, including immersion cooling technology and energy harvesting initiatives.
NVDA: NVIDIA Corporation is the world's leading designer of graphics processing units (GPUs) and a dominant force in accelerated computing. Originally focused on gaming graphics, NVIDIA has become the most important company in the AI revolution, with its data center GPUs powering the vast majority of AI training and inference workloads globally. The company's CUDA software platform and ecosystem create a significant competitive moat. NVIDIA's market capitalization has made it one of the most valuable companies in the world.
NXPI: NXP Semiconductors is a global leader in secure connectivity solutions for embedded applications. The company provides semiconductor solutions for automotive, industrial, IoT, mobile, and communications infrastructure markets. NXP is the #1 semiconductor supplier to the automotive industry and a leader in secure identification, NFC, and RFID technology. The company's products are essential for advanced driver assistance systems, vehicle electrification, and the connected car ecosystem.
OKE: ONEOK, Inc. is one of the largest operators of natural gas gathering, processing, and transportation infrastructure in the United States. The company's extensive pipeline network connects key supply basins to major market centers across the Midcontinent and Rocky Mountain regions. ONEOK provides critical midstream services that support natural gas and NGL production. The company is known for its fee-based business model, strong distribution coverage, and consistent growth through infrastructure expansion.
PDD: PDD Holdings is a multinational commerce group that operates two major e-commerce platforms: Pinduoduo in China and Temu internationally. Pinduoduo revolutionized Chinese e-commerce with its social commerce and group-buying model, becoming one of the largest e-commerce platforms in China by users. Temu, launched in 2022, has rapidly expanded globally with an ultra-low-price direct-from-factory model, reaching hundreds of millions of users across North America, Europe, and other markets.
HOOD: Robinhood Markets is a financial services company that pioneered commission-free stock trading through its mobile app. The company offers trading in stocks, ETFs, options, and cryptocurrencies, as well as cash management and retirement accounts. Robinhood's mission is to democratize finance for all, and its easy-to-use platform has attracted a large base of younger, first-time investors. The company has expanded into gold subscriptions, credit cards, and wealth management services.
SYF: Synchrony Financial is one of the premier consumer financial services companies in the United States. The company provides a range of credit products through programs established with retailers, healthcare providers, auto dealers, and digital partners. Synchrony is the largest provider of private label credit cards in the U.S., partnering with major brands including Amazon, Lowe's, PayPal, and Walgreens. The company leverages data analytics and digital capabilities to drive engagement and growth.
TSM: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company is the world's largest dedicated semiconductor foundry, manufacturing chips designed by other companies. TSMC produces the most advanced chips in the world, including processors for Apple, NVIDIA, AMD, and Qualcomm. The company holds approximately 60% of the global foundry market share and dominates leading-edge chip production. TSMC's technology leadership in advanced process nodes (3nm, 5nm) makes it one of the most strategically important companies in the global technology supply chain.
TOL: Toll Brothers is the nation's leading builder of luxury homes, operating in 24 states across the United States. The company builds single-family detached and attached homes, master-planned communities, and urban high-rise condominiums. Toll Brothers targets the move-up and luxury segments of the housing market, with an average home selling price significantly above the national median. The company also operates mortgage, title, and insurance subsidiaries.
IBIT: iShares Bitcoin Trust is a spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund managed by BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager. Launched in January 2024, IBIT provides investors with direct exposure to Bitcoin through a regulated, exchange-traded vehicle without the need to directly hold or custody the cryptocurrency. IBIT has become one of the fastest-growing ETFs in history, attracting tens of billions in assets within its first year of trading.
ETHA: iShares Ethereum Trust is a spot Ethereum exchange-traded fund managed by BlackRock. Launched in 2024, ETHA provides investors with direct exposure to Ethereum, the second-largest cryptocurrency by market capitalization, through a regulated exchange-traded vehicle. Ethereum is a decentralized blockchain platform that enables smart contracts and decentralized applications (dApps), serving as the foundation for much of the decentralized finance (DeFi) ecosystem.
IUSG: iShares Core S&P U.S. Growth ETF tracks the S&P 900 Growth Index, providing broad exposure to large- and mid-cap U.S. growth stocks. The fund emphasizes companies exhibiting above-average growth characteristics including sales growth, earnings growth, and price momentum. IUSG is one of the lowest-cost growth ETFs available, with a heavy weighting toward technology, consumer discretionary, and healthcare sectors.
DVY: iShares Select Dividend ETF tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Select Dividend Index, providing exposure to relatively high-dividend-paying U.S. equities. The fund selects stocks based on dividend yield, dividend growth rate, and payout ratio, screening for quality and sustainability. DVY offers diversified exposure across sectors including utilities, financials, energy, and consumer staples, making it a popular choice for income-focused investors.
IWS: iShares Russell Mid-Cap Value ETF tracks the Russell Midcap Value Index, providing exposure to mid-sized U.S. companies exhibiting value characteristics. The fund targets companies with lower price-to-book ratios and lower expected growth rates relative to the broader mid-cap market. IWS offers diversified exposure across sectors including financials, industrials, real estate, and healthcare, providing a complement to growth-oriented mid-cap strategies.
SPY: SPDR S&P 500 ETF Trust is the world's first and largest exchange-traded fund, tracking the S&P 500 Index. Launched in 1993, SPY provides broad exposure to 500 of the largest U.S. companies, representing approximately 80% of total U.S. equity market capitalization. It is the most actively traded security in the world by dollar volume and serves as the primary benchmark for U.S. large-cap equity performance.
QQQ: Invesco QQQ Trust tracks the Nasdaq-100 Index, providing exposure to 100 of the largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq stock exchange. The fund is heavily weighted toward technology and growth-oriented companies including Apple, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Amazon, and Meta. QQQ is one of the most actively traded ETFs in the world and is widely used as a benchmark for large-cap growth and technology sector performance.
DIA: SPDR Dow Jones Industrial Average ETF Trust tracks the Dow Jones Industrial Average, one of the oldest and most widely recognized stock market indices in the world. The fund provides exposure to 30 large, well-established U.S. companies across various industries, selected by the editors of The Wall Street Journal. DIA is a price-weighted index, meaning higher-priced stocks have greater influence on the index's performance.
NTR: Nutrien Ltd. is the world's largest provider of crop inputs and services, producing and distributing nitrogen, potash, and phosphate fertilizers. Headquartered in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, the company operates extensive mining and manufacturing facilities across North America and owns the largest agricultural retail network globally, with approximately 2,000 farm supply locations. Nutrien plays a critical role in global food security, as its products underpin roughly half of the world's crop yields.
CTRA: Coterra Energy Inc. is an independent oil and natural gas exploration and production company operating in two of America's premier basins: the Permian Basin in West Texas (oil-focused) and the Marcellus Shale in Appalachia (natural gas-focused). This dual-basin strategy provides diversified exposure across both oil and gas commodity cycles. The company is known for disciplined capital allocation, low-cost operations, and a shareholder-friendly return framework that combines a base dividend with variable distributions.
FCX: Freeport-McMoRan Inc. is the world's largest publicly traded copper mining company, operating the massive Grasberg mine in Indonesia — one of the largest copper and gold deposits on earth — alongside significant operations in Arizona and Peru. Copper is essential to electrification, renewable energy, electric vehicles, and data center power infrastructure. With new copper mines requiring 10-15 years to develop, Freeport's existing production capacity positions it as a critical supplier in a structurally supply-constrained market.
CRDO: Credo Technology Group designs and sells high-speed connectivity semiconductors for data centers. The company's SerDes (serializer/deserializer) chips and active electrical cables enable data to move between GPUs and switches at extreme speeds inside AI training clusters. As AI data centers scale to hundreds of thousands of processors, the interconnect fabric between them — not the processors themselves — becomes the performance bottleneck. Credo's products sit at exactly that chokepoint, driving revenue from $107 million to over $1.3 billion in annual run rate in approximately three years.
VST: Vistra Corp. is one of the largest independent power producers in the United States, operating a diverse fleet of natural gas, nuclear, coal, and renewable generation assets. The company owns the second-largest competitive nuclear fleet in the country, providing 24/7 zero-emission baseload power. With U.S. electricity demand expected to grow 50% by 2040 driven by AI data centers, manufacturing reshoring, and electric vehicles, Vistra has secured 20-year power purchase agreements with major technology companies including Meta and Amazon for over 2,600 megawatts of nuclear capacity.
MRVL: Marvell Technology Inc. is a leading semiconductor company focused on data infrastructure. Approximately three-quarters of its revenue comes from data center customers, where Marvell designs custom AI accelerator chips (XPUs) for hyperscale cloud companies including Alphabet, Amazon, and Microsoft. The company also produces industry-standard PAM4 DSP chips that convert data between electrical and optical signals — critical technology as data centers transition from copper to fiber optic interconnects. Marvell's acquisition of Celestial AI adds photonic fabric technology that uses light to move data between chips on the same board.
AAPL: Apple Inc. is the world's most valuable company, designing and selling consumer electronics, software, and services. Its ecosystem of iPhone, Mac, iPad, Apple Watch, and services (App Store, Apple Music, iCloud, Apple Pay) generates over $380 billion in annual revenue with industry-leading profit margins. Apple's installed base of over 2 billion active devices creates a powerful recurring revenue flywheel through services, which now accounts for over 25% of revenue at significantly higher margins than hardware.
ADBE: Adobe Inc. is the global leader in creative and digital experience software, with products like Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere Pro, and Acrobat defining industry standards across design, video, photography, and document management. The company's transition to a cloud subscription model (Creative Cloud, Document Cloud, Experience Cloud) has created one of the most predictable revenue streams in enterprise software, with over 95% recurring revenue.
AGI: Alamos Gold Inc. is a Canadian-based intermediate gold producer with diversified operations in North America. The company operates the Young-Davidson and Island Gold mines in Ontario, Canada, and the Mulatos mine in Sonora, Mexico. Alamos has a strong track record of reserve replacement and mine life extension, with Island Gold emerging as one of the highest-grade, lowest-cost underground gold mines in the world.
ALAB: Astera Labs designs and sells semiconductor-based connectivity solutions for cloud and AI infrastructure. The company specializes in intelligent connectivity platform ICs that address data, network, and memory connectivity bottlenecks in cloud and AI data centers. Its products enable reliable, high-speed data transfer between servers, storage, and network equipment at hyperscale.
AMAT: Applied Materials is the world's largest supplier of semiconductor manufacturing equipment, providing the machines, software, and services that chipmakers use to produce virtually every chip in the world. The company's products span deposition, etch, ion implantation, and inspection — critical steps in manufacturing advanced semiconductors. With AI driving demand for more complex chips, Applied Materials sits at the center of the semiconductor supply chain.
AMGN: Amgen Inc. is one of the world's largest biotechnology companies, pioneering the development of biologic medicines for serious illnesses. The company's portfolio includes blockbuster drugs in oncology, cardiovascular disease, bone health, and inflammation. Amgen's biosimilar portfolio and pipeline of novel therapies, including obesity treatments, position it for sustained growth.
AMZN: Amazon.com is the world's largest e-commerce company and a dominant force in cloud computing through Amazon Web Services (AWS). AWS generates the majority of Amazon's operating profit and holds approximately 31% of the global cloud infrastructure market. The company also operates in advertising, streaming (Prime Video), logistics, and AI services, creating one of the most diversified technology conglomerates in history.
ANET: Arista Networks is a leading provider of cloud networking solutions for large-scale data centers, campus environments, and routing applications. The company's software-driven approach to networking, built on its Extensible Operating System (EOS), has made it the preferred networking vendor for hyperscale cloud providers and AI infrastructure buildouts. Arista holds approximately 25% of the high-speed data center switching market.
APH: Amphenol Corporation is one of the world's largest manufacturers of electronic and fiber optic connectors, cable assemblies, and interconnect systems. The company serves virtually every end market including defense, automotive, broadband, industrial, mobile, and data center applications. Amphenol's diversified exposure across over 100,000 customers in 70+ countries provides exceptional revenue stability.
ARM: Arm Holdings designs and licenses semiconductor intellectual property (IP) that powers over 99% of the world's smartphones and is increasingly critical for data centers, automotive, and IoT applications. Rather than manufacturing chips, Arm licenses its CPU architecture to companies like Apple, Qualcomm, NVIDIA, and Samsung, earning royalties on every chip shipped. The company's energy-efficient designs are essential for AI edge computing.
ASML: ASML Holding is the world's sole manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines, which are essential for producing the most advanced semiconductor chips. No EUV machine, no leading-edge chip — giving ASML an unparalleled monopoly in the semiconductor equipment industry. Each EUV system costs over $200 million, and the company has a multi-year order backlog.
AVGO: Broadcom Inc. is a global technology leader that designs, develops, and supplies semiconductor and infrastructure software solutions. The company's chips are critical for networking, broadband, storage, and wireless communications. Following its acquisition of VMware, Broadcom has become a major force in enterprise infrastructure software, creating a diversified hardware-software conglomerate.
AWK: American Water Works Company is the largest publicly traded U.S. water and wastewater utility, serving approximately 14 million people across 14 states. The company operates regulated water utilities that benefit from predictable, inflation-protected rate increases approved by state regulators. Water infrastructure in the U.S. requires massive reinvestment, providing a long runway for capital deployment and rate base growth.
AZN: AstraZeneca PLC is a global biopharmaceutical company with a diversified portfolio spanning oncology, cardiovascular, respiratory, immunology, and rare diseases. The company has undergone a remarkable transformation, rebuilding its pipeline through internal R&D and strategic acquisitions. AstraZeneca's oncology franchise, including Tagrisso, Imfinzi, and Enhertu, is among the strongest in the industry.
BAM: Brookfield Asset Management is one of the world's largest alternative asset managers, with over $900 billion in assets under management across renewable energy, infrastructure, real estate, private equity, and credit. The company earns fee-related earnings from managing third-party capital and carried interest from investment performance, creating a capital-light, high-margin business model.
BE: Bloom Energy Corporation designs, manufactures, and sells solid-oxide fuel cell systems that produce electricity on-site with significantly lower emissions than traditional power generation. The company's Energy Servers convert natural gas or hydrogen into electricity through an electrochemical process, serving data centers, hospitals, manufacturing facilities, and utilities seeking reliable, distributed power.
BSY: Bentley Systems is a leading provider of infrastructure engineering software for the design, construction, and operations of bridges, roads, buildings, utilities, and industrial facilities. The company's software platform enables digital twins — virtual replicas of physical infrastructure — helping engineers and operators improve project delivery and asset performance throughout the infrastructure lifecycle.
CB: Chubb Limited is the world's largest publicly traded property and casualty insurance company, with operations in 54 countries. The company underwrites commercial and personal insurance, providing coverage for businesses, high-net-worth individuals, and consumers. Chubb's disciplined underwriting culture consistently delivers industry-leading combined ratios and return on equity.
CDNS: Cadence Design Systems provides electronic design automation (EDA) software and hardware used to design semiconductors, printed circuit boards, and electronic systems. The company's tools are essential for chip designers at companies like NVIDIA, Apple, and AMD to create increasingly complex integrated circuits. With chip complexity growing exponentially for AI, Cadence's tools are mission-critical.
CEG: Constellation Energy Corporation is the nation's largest producer of carbon-free energy, operating a fleet of nuclear, wind, solar, and hydroelectric generation assets. The company's nuclear fleet provides reliable baseload power that is increasingly valued by hyperscale data center operators seeking 24/7 clean energy. Constellation's power purchase agreements with major tech companies provide revenue visibility.
CLBT: Cellebrite DI Ltd. provides digital intelligence solutions for public safety and enterprise customers. The company's technology enables law enforcement and intelligence agencies to legally extract, analyze, and manage digital data from mobile devices and other digital sources. Cellebrite's solutions are used by over 6,700 public safety agencies and enterprises worldwide.
CLS: Celestica Inc. is a global leader in electronics manufacturing services (EMS) and supply chain solutions, serving the communications, enterprise computing, aerospace and defense, and industrial markets. The company has emerged as a key beneficiary of AI infrastructure buildout, manufacturing networking equipment and server components for hyperscale data center operators.
CNI: Canadian National Railway Company operates the largest rail network in Canada and the only transcontinental network in North America, spanning approximately 20,000 route miles. The company transports commodities including petroleum, grain, forest products, coal, and intermodal containers across Canada and into the U.S. Gulf Coast, providing critical supply chain infrastructure.
COST: Costco Wholesale Corporation operates a chain of membership-only warehouse clubs, offering a limited selection of products at exceptionally low prices. The company's membership model, with over 130 million cardholders worldwide, generates highly predictable recurring revenue while driving customer loyalty. Costco's 90%+ membership renewal rate and expanding e-commerce presence support continued growth.
CP: Canadian Pacific Kansas City Limited is the only single-line railroad connecting Canada, the United States, and Mexico following the transformative merger of Canadian Pacific and Kansas City Southern. The combined network spans approximately 20,000 miles across all three North American countries, creating unique competitive advantages for cross-border trade.
CPRT: Copart Inc. operates the world's largest online vehicle auction platform, specializing in salvage and clean title vehicles. The company processes over 4 million vehicles annually through its 250+ locations across 11 countries. Copart's virtual auction platform, VB3, has transformed the global vehicle remarketing industry, connecting sellers with over 750,000 registered buyers worldwide.
CRM: Salesforce is the world's leading customer relationship management (CRM) platform, serving over 150,000 companies worldwide. The company's cloud-based suite includes Sales Cloud, Service Cloud, Marketing Cloud, and its AI platform Einstein, enabling businesses to manage customer interactions across every touchpoint. Salesforce's acquisition of Slack and Tableau has expanded its enterprise collaboration and analytics capabilities.
CSCO: Cisco Systems is the worldwide leader in networking equipment and enterprise infrastructure technology. The company's switches, routers, and security appliances form the backbone of the internet and corporate networks globally. Cisco has successfully transitioned to a software and subscription-driven model, with recurring revenue now representing over 50% of total revenue.
DDOG: Datadog Inc. provides a cloud-based monitoring and analytics platform for developers, IT operations teams, and business users. The company's unified platform combines infrastructure monitoring, application performance management, log management, and security monitoring, enabling organizations to observe their entire technology stack. Datadog's land-and-expand model drives strong net revenue retention.
DE: Deere & Company is the world's largest manufacturer of agricultural equipment and a major producer of construction, forestry, and turf care machinery. The company's precision agriculture technology platform, including GPS guidance, autonomous tractors, and data analytics, is transforming farming productivity. Deere's technology moat and global dealer network create significant competitive advantages.
DECK: Deckers Outdoor Corporation designs and markets premium footwear and apparel brands including UGG, HOKA, and Teva. HOKA has emerged as one of the fastest-growing athletic footwear brands globally, expanding from running into lifestyle and trail categories. The company's direct-to-consumer strategy and brand management have driven exceptional margin expansion.
DOV: Dover Corporation is a diversified global industrial manufacturer with five operating segments: engineered products, clean energy and fueling, imaging and identification, pumps and process solutions, and climate and sustainability technologies. The company's products serve attractive end markets including clean energy, biopharma, and industrial automation.
DT: Dynatrace Inc. provides a software intelligence platform that uses AI and automation to monitor and optimize the performance of applications, cloud infrastructure, and digital experiences. The company's platform processes trillions of dependency data points per day, providing enterprise customers with actionable insights to ensure software reliability and performance.
ECL: Ecolab Inc. is the global leader in water treatment, hygiene, and infection prevention solutions. The company serves over 3 million customer locations in more than 170 countries across food service, healthcare, hospitality, and industrial markets. Ecolab's subscription-like service model, with on-site dispensing systems and recurring chemical supplies, generates predictable revenue with high switching costs.
EMBJ: Embraer S.A. is the world's third-largest commercial aircraft manufacturer and a leading producer of executive jets, military aircraft, and defense systems. Based in Brazil, the company's E-Jet family of regional aircraft has captured significant market share in the 70-150 seat segment. Embraer's defense division produces the KC-390 military transport aircraft and the Super Tucano light attack aircraft.
ETN: Eaton Corporation is a global power management company providing energy-efficient solutions across electrical, aerospace, vehicle, and eMobility sectors. The company's electrical segment, its largest, manufactures circuit breakers, transformers, and power distribution equipment critical for data center power infrastructure. Eaton is a key beneficiary of electrification and AI-driven power demand growth.
FIG: Figma Inc. is a cloud-based collaborative design platform used by product teams to create user interfaces, prototypes, and design systems. The company's browser-based approach enables real-time collaboration among designers, developers, and stakeholders, disrupting traditional desktop design tools. Figma has become the industry standard for product design at technology companies.
GE: GE Aerospace is a pure-play aviation company and one of the world's leading jet engine manufacturers. Following the separation from GE's legacy conglomerate, GE Aerospace focuses exclusively on designing, manufacturing, and servicing jet engines and related components for commercial and military aircraft. The company's LEAP engine program, developed jointly with Safran, powers the majority of new narrow-body aircraft.
GEV: GE Vernova is a global energy company focused on the electrification, power, and wind segments. Spun off from General Electric, the company is one of the world's largest providers of power generation equipment, including gas turbines, wind turbines, and grid solutions. GE Vernova is positioned at the center of the global energy transition and the growing need for reliable power generation.
GLW: Corning Incorporated is a leading innovator in materials science, producing specialty glass, ceramics, and optical physics products. The company's five market-access platforms — optical communications, display technologies, specialty materials, environmental technologies, and life sciences — serve diverse end markets. Corning's optical fiber business is a key beneficiary of AI-driven data center fiber demand.
GMAB: Genmab A/S is a Danish biotechnology company focused on creating and developing differentiated antibody therapeutics for cancer and other serious diseases. The company's proprietary antibody technology platforms have produced multiple approved therapies, including Darzalex (daratumumab) for multiple myeloma, one of the best-selling cancer drugs globally, developed in partnership with Johnson & Johnson.
GOOG: Alphabet Inc. (Class C shares) is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine controlling over 90% of global search traffic. The company also owns YouTube, Google Cloud, Android, and Waymo autonomous vehicles. Google's advertising business generates over $200 billion annually, while Google Cloud is one of the three major cloud computing platforms alongside AWS and Azure.
GOOGL: Alphabet Inc. (Class A shares) is the parent company of Google, the world's dominant search engine and digital advertising platform. Beyond search, Alphabet operates YouTube (the world's largest video platform), Google Cloud (a top-three cloud provider), Android (powering 72% of global smartphones), and Waymo (a leader in autonomous driving). The company's AI capabilities, including Gemini, are being integrated across all products.
HD: The Home Depot is the world's largest home improvement retailer, operating over 2,300 stores across North America. The company serves both do-it-yourself consumers and professional contractors, with Pro customers representing approximately 50% of sales. Home Depot's scale advantages in sourcing, distribution, and digital capabilities create significant competitive moats in a fragmented industry.
HLT: Hilton Worldwide Holdings is one of the largest hospitality companies in the world, with a portfolio of 22 brands spanning approximately 7,600 properties across 126 countries. The company operates an asset-light franchise model, with over 80% of its rooms managed or franchised, generating high-margin fee revenue with minimal capital requirements. Hilton's loyalty program, Hilton Honors, has over 190 million members.
IBN: ICICI Bank Limited is one of India's largest private sector banks by total assets, providing a comprehensive range of banking products and financial services. The bank serves retail, SME, and corporate customers through an extensive network of branches and digital platforms across India. ICICI Bank's digital transformation and India's growing middle class provide a long runway for growth.
ICE: Intercontinental Exchange operates global financial exchanges and clearing houses, including the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE), ICE Futures, and ICE Clear. The company also provides fixed income and data services, mortgage technology, and indices. ICE's diversified exchange and data business benefits from secular growth in global trading volumes and financial data consumption.
INOD: Innodata Inc. is a global data engineering and AI company that provides data annotation, data transformation, and AI/ML model development services. The company helps enterprises prepare and manage the massive datasets required to train and deploy AI systems. Innodata's human-in-the-loop approach to data labeling serves major technology companies building large language models and AI applications.
INTU: Intuit Inc. is the creator of TurboTax, QuickBooks, and Mailchimp — platforms that serve over 100 million consumers and small businesses worldwide. The company's AI-powered financial platform helps individuals prepare taxes, small businesses manage finances, and marketers reach customers. Intuit's platform strategy creates powerful network effects and high switching costs.
ISRG: Intuitive Surgical is the global leader in robotic-assisted, minimally invasive surgery, with its da Vinci surgical system installed in over 8,500 hospitals worldwide. The company's recurring revenue from instruments, accessories, and service contracts represents approximately 80% of total revenue. With only 3% of surgeries performed robotically, Intuitive has a massive addressable market ahead.
JNJ: Johnson & Johnson is one of the world's largest healthcare companies, with operations spanning pharmaceuticals, medical devices, and consumer health. Following the separation of its consumer health business (Kenvue), J&J is focused on its higher-growth pharmaceutical and medical technology segments. The company's pharmaceutical pipeline includes over 100 drug candidates across oncology, immunology, and neuroscience.
JPM: JPMorgan Chase & Co. is the largest bank in the United States and one of the largest financial institutions in the world by assets. The company operates across four segments: consumer and community banking, corporate and investment banking, commercial banking, and asset and wealth management. JPMorgan's scale, technology investments, and fortress balance sheet provide significant competitive advantages.
KKR: KKR & Co. Inc. is a leading global investment firm managing approximately $553 billion in assets across private equity, credit, real assets, and insurance. The company earns management fees, transaction fees, and carried interest from its investment activities. KKR's expansion into insurance through Global Atlantic has added a permanent capital base and stable fee streams.
KLAC: KLA Corporation is a leading supplier of process control and yield management equipment for the semiconductor industry. The company's inspection and metrology tools are essential for detecting and measuring defects during chip manufacturing, becoming increasingly critical as chip geometries shrink. KLA holds dominant market share in wafer inspection, with its tools used in virtually every semiconductor fab worldwide.
KTOS: Kratos Defense & Security Solutions provides mission-critical technology products and solutions for national security. The company specializes in unmanned aerial systems (drones), satellite communications, cybersecurity, and microwave electronics for defense applications. Kratos's affordable, attritable drone platforms are positioned to benefit from the U.S. military's shift toward unmanned combat systems.
LIN: Linde plc is the world's largest industrial gases company, supplying oxygen, nitrogen, argon, hydrogen, and other specialty gases to customers across healthcare, manufacturing, food processing, electronics, and energy industries. The company's global distribution network and long-term take-or-pay contracts create a highly resilient business model with predictable cash flows.
LITE: Lumentum Holdings manufactures photonic and optical products for communications, commercial lasers, and 3D sensing applications. The company's products are critical for fiber optic network infrastructure, enabling high-speed data transmission in telecommunications and data center networks. Lumentum is positioned to benefit from AI-driven demand for higher-bandwidth optical interconnects.
LLY: Eli Lilly and Company is a global pharmaceutical company that has emerged as a leader in diabetes, obesity, oncology, and neuroscience. The company's GLP-1 receptor agonists — Mounjaro (tirzepatide) for diabetes and Zepbound for obesity — represent a potential $100+ billion market opportunity. Lilly's market capitalization has surged past $700 billion on the strength of its obesity and Alzheimer's pipeline.
LMND: Lemonade Inc. is a technology-driven insurance company offering homeowners, renters, pet, car, and life insurance through a digital-first platform powered by AI and behavioral economics. The company's AI-powered claims processing and underwriting aim to reduce costs and improve customer experience. Lemonade's growth is driven by its ability to attract younger, digital-native customers.
LNG: Cheniere Energy is the largest producer and exporter of liquefied natural gas (LNG) in the United States, operating the Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi liquefaction facilities. The company's long-term, take-or-pay contracts with global buyers provide highly predictable cash flows. With the Iran War disrupting global gas supply chains, Cheniere's strategic importance has increased significantly.
MA: Mastercard Incorporated is one of the world's two dominant payment networks, processing transactions across more than 210 countries and territories. The company operates a capital-light network model, earning fees on every transaction that flows through its rails without taking credit risk. Mastercard's expansion into cross-border payments, cybersecurity, and data analytics diversifies revenue beyond card payments.
MBLY: Mobileye Global Inc. is a leader in autonomous driving technology and advanced driver-assistance systems (ADAS). A subsidiary of Intel, Mobileye's EyeQ chips and software are used by over 50 automakers in more than 150 million vehicles worldwide. The company's camera-first approach to self-driving, combined with its REM crowdsourced mapping platform, provides a differentiated path to autonomous mobility.
MCD: McDonald's Corporation is the world's largest fast-food restaurant chain, with approximately 40,000 restaurants in over 100 countries. Over 95% of McDonald's restaurants are franchised, creating a capital-light business model that generates predictable fee-based revenue. The company's scale in purchasing, real estate, and marketing provides significant competitive advantages that are difficult to replicate.
MDA: MDA Space Ltd. is a Canadian space technology company providing robotics, satellite systems, and geointelligence solutions for commercial and government customers. The company designed and built the Canadarm robotic systems for NASA's Space Shuttle and International Space Station programs. MDA's satellite constellation capabilities and space servicing technologies position it in the growing commercial space economy.
META: Meta Platforms is the world's largest social media company, operating Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and Messenger with over 3.9 billion monthly active users combined. The company generates over $130 billion annually in advertising revenue through its precision-targeted digital ad platform. Meta's massive investment in AI and its Reality Labs division (Quest VR headsets, smart glasses) represent bets on the next computing platform.
MOD: Modine Manufacturing Company is a global leader in thermal management technology, providing heating, cooling, and ventilation solutions for data centers, commercial vehicles, and industrial applications. The company's data center cooling products have become a high-growth segment as AI workloads generate increasing amounts of heat that require sophisticated thermal management solutions.
MSFT: Microsoft Corporation is the world's second-most valuable company, with dominant positions in enterprise software (Office 365, Azure, Dynamics), cloud computing, gaming (Xbox), and AI (Copilot, OpenAI partnership). Azure is the second-largest cloud platform globally with approximately 25% market share. Microsoft's integration of AI across its product portfolio, including GitHub Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot, positions it as a primary beneficiary of enterprise AI adoption.
MSI: Motorola Solutions provides mission-critical communication infrastructure and devices for public safety and enterprise customers. The company's land mobile radio systems, body-worn cameras, and command center software serve over 100,000 public safety and commercial customers in more than 100 countries. Motorola Solutions' recurring software and services revenue provides high visibility.
MU: Micron Technology is one of the world's largest manufacturers of memory and storage semiconductors, producing DRAM and NAND flash chips used in data centers, smartphones, PCs, and automotive applications. The company's high-bandwidth memory (HBM) products are critical for AI training and inference workloads, creating a new high-margin growth driver alongside the traditional memory cycle.
NBIX: Neurocrine Biosciences is a neurology-focused biopharmaceutical company with a growing portfolio of therapies for neurological, neuroendocrine, and neuropsychiatric disorders. The company's lead product, Ingrezza (valbenazine), is the first FDA-approved treatment for tardive dyskinesia and has become a blockbuster drug. Neurocrine's pipeline addresses significant unmet medical needs in movement disorders and psychiatric conditions.
NFLX: Netflix Inc. is the world's largest streaming entertainment service with over 280 million paid memberships in more than 190 countries. The company produces and distributes original content across films, series, documentaries, and games, spending over $17 billion annually on content. Netflix's ad-supported tier and password-sharing crackdown have opened significant new revenue and subscriber growth opportunities.
NOW: ServiceNow is a leading enterprise cloud platform for digital workflow automation. The company's IT Service Management (ITSM) platform has expanded into IT operations, HR service delivery, customer service, and security operations, creating a unified platform for enterprise digital transformation. ServiceNow's platform is used by over 80% of Fortune 500 companies.
NRG: NRG Energy is one of the largest integrated power companies in the United States, generating and selling electricity to residential, commercial, and industrial customers. The company operates a diversified generation fleet including natural gas, nuclear, coal, oil, solar, and wind facilities. NRG's retail electricity brands serve approximately 7.5 million customers across multiple states.
NU: Nu Holdings is a Brazilian digital financial services company and one of the world's largest neobanks, serving over 90 million customers across Brazil, Mexico, and Colombia. The company offers a full suite of financial products including credit cards, personal loans, savings accounts, insurance, and investment products through its mobile app. Nu's cost advantage over traditional Latin American banks drives rapid customer acquisition.
NVT: nVent Electric plc designs and manufactures electrical connection and protection solutions for critical infrastructure applications. The company's products — including enclosures, heat tracing, and electrical connections — protect sensitive electronics and equipment in data centers, industrial facilities, and commercial buildings. nVent's data center cooling and power distribution products are benefiting from AI infrastructure buildout.
NXT: Nextpower Inc. is a next-generation energy company focused on distributed power solutions and clean energy infrastructure. The company develops, owns, and operates clean energy projects, providing distributed generation and energy storage solutions for commercial and industrial customers seeking reliable, sustainable power.
ORCL: Oracle Corporation is a global enterprise technology company providing cloud infrastructure, database management, enterprise applications, and AI services. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) has emerged as a fourth major cloud platform, winning workloads from large enterprises seeking alternatives to AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud. The company's autonomous database and AI-optimized cloud architecture differentiate it in the enterprise market.
PANW: Palo Alto Networks is the world's largest pure-play cybersecurity company, providing next-generation firewalls, cloud security, and AI-powered threat detection. The company's platformization strategy — consolidating customers' security tools onto its unified platform — drives strong net revenue retention and wallet share expansion. With cyber threats accelerating globally, Palo Alto's TAM continues to expand.
PGR: The Progressive Corporation is one of the largest auto insurance providers in the United States, known for its data-driven underwriting and pricing models. The company's Snapshot usage-based insurance program and direct-to-consumer distribution model have driven consistent market share gains. Progressive's combined ratio discipline and digital capabilities make it one of the most efficient P&C insurers.
PLTR: Palantir Technologies builds software platforms for data integration and analysis, serving both government intelligence agencies and commercial enterprises. The company's Gotham platform (government) and Foundry platform (commercial) enable organizations to integrate, manage, and analyze large datasets. Palantir's AI Platform (AIP) has driven accelerating commercial growth as enterprises adopt AI-powered decision-making.
PNFP: Pinnacle Financial Partners is a Nashville-based financial holding company known for its relationship-driven banking model. The company serves commercial and private banking clients in high-growth Southeastern U.S. markets including Nashville, Memphis, Atlanta, and Washington D.C. Pinnacle's culture-first approach to banking has earned it consistent recognition as one of the best workplaces in financial services.
PTC: PTC Inc. provides industrial software solutions for product lifecycle management (PLM), computer-aided design (CAD), Internet of Things (IoT), and augmented reality (AR). The company's Windchill PLM and Creo CAD platforms are used by manufacturers worldwide to design, develop, and service complex products. PTC's IoT platform, ThingWorx, enables digital transformation in discrete manufacturing.
PWR: Quanta Services is the largest specialty contractor in North America, providing infrastructure services for the electric power, oil and gas, and telecommunications industries. The company builds, installs, and maintains the infrastructure networks that deliver electricity, oil, gas, and telecommunications services. Quanta is a primary beneficiary of grid modernization, renewable energy buildout, and 5G infrastructure deployment.
RCL: Royal Caribbean Cruises Ltd. is one of the world's largest cruise companies, operating five brands including Royal Caribbean International, Celebrity Cruises, and Silversea. The company's fleet of approximately 65 ships serves millions of guests annually across destinations worldwide. Royal Caribbean's yield management, onboard revenue optimization, and new ship deliveries drive consistent earnings growth.
RMBS: Rambus Inc. is a semiconductor and IP licensing company specializing in high-speed memory interface and security technologies. The company's products and technologies are used in data centers, government applications, and consumer devices. Rambus's memory interface chips are critical for enabling high-bandwidth data transfer in server memory systems, becoming increasingly important for AI workloads.
RMD: ResMed Inc. is the global leader in cloud-connected medical devices for the treatment of sleep apnea and respiratory care. The company's CPAP machines, masks, and digital health platform serve over 160 million patients in more than 140 countries. ResMed's connected device ecosystem generates valuable clinical data that improves patient outcomes and creates recurring revenue through mask replacements and software subscriptions.
SAP: SAP SE is the world's largest enterprise application software company, providing ERP (enterprise resource planning), supply chain management, human capital management, and business intelligence solutions. The company serves over 400,000 customers in 190 countries, with its software running 87% of total global commerce. SAP's cloud transformation under CEO Christian Klein has accelerated growth.
SCHW: The Charles Schwab Corporation is one of the largest brokerage and banking firms in the United States, serving over 35 million active accounts with approximately $8 trillion in client assets. The company's zero-commission trading model, combined with its RIA custody platform and banking services, creates a comprehensive wealth management ecosystem. Schwab's scale advantages in cost per account are unmatched.
SE: Sea Limited is a Singapore-based internet conglomerate operating in digital entertainment (Garena), e-commerce (Shopee), and digital financial services (SeaMoney) across Southeast Asia, Taiwan, Brazil, and other markets. Shopee is the leading e-commerce platform in Southeast Asia by order volume, while SeaMoney provides digital payments and financial services to underbanked populations.
SERV: Serve Robotics Inc. designs and operates autonomous sidewalk delivery robots for the food delivery and e-commerce industries. The company's robots use advanced AI, computer vision, and sensor technology to navigate urban environments and deliver goods safely. Serve partners with platforms like Uber Eats to provide last-mile delivery, aiming to reduce delivery costs while improving sustainability.
SHOP: Shopify Inc. is the leading commerce platform enabling millions of merchants worldwide to sell products online, in-store, and across social media. The company provides a complete e-commerce infrastructure including website hosting, payment processing, shipping, and marketing tools. Shopify's platform powers over 10% of U.S. e-commerce, making it the second-largest online retail platform after Amazon.
SNPS: Synopsys Inc. is a leading provider of electronic design automation (EDA) software and semiconductor IP. The company's tools are used to design and verify advanced integrated circuits, from initial architecture through manufacturing. Together with Cadence, Synopsys forms a duopoly in the EDA market, with their tools essential for designing virtually every semiconductor chip in the world.
SPGI: S&P Global Inc. provides credit ratings, benchmarks, analytics, and data services to the global financial markets. The company's divisions include S&P Global Ratings (one of three dominant credit rating agencies), S&P Dow Jones Indices (including the S&P 500), S&P Global Market Intelligence, and S&P Global Commodity Insights. The merger with IHS Markit created a data and analytics powerhouse.
TOST: Toast Inc. provides a cloud-based digital technology platform for the restaurant industry. The company's integrated suite includes point-of-sale systems, online ordering, delivery management, payroll, and marketing tools specifically designed for restaurants. Toast serves over 100,000 restaurant locations across the United States, processing over $130 billion in gross payment volume annually.
TTMI: TTM Technologies is a leading global printed circuit board (PCB) manufacturer, producing complex multilayer PCBs and RF components for aerospace and defense, automotive, data center, medical, and industrial applications. The company's advanced technology PCBs are critical components in military radar systems, satellite communications, networking equipment, and AI server infrastructure.
TXN: Texas Instruments Incorporated is the world's largest maker of analog semiconductors and a major producer of embedded processing chips. The company's analog chips convert real-world signals (temperature, sound, pressure) into digital data, serving over 100,000 customers across industrial, automotive, personal electronics, and communications markets. TI's manufacturing scale and 300mm wafer production provide significant cost advantages.
VEEV: Veeva Systems provides cloud-based software for the global life sciences industry, serving pharmaceutical, biotech, and medical device companies. The company's platform includes CRM, clinical data management, regulatory compliance, and quality management solutions specifically designed for life sciences workflows. Veeva's industry-specific focus has created deep competitive moats with over 1,000 customer organizations.
VIST: Vista Energy S.A.B. de C.V. is an independent oil and gas company focused on the development of unconventional resources in the Vaca Muerta shale formation in Argentina. The company is one of the largest oil producers in Argentina, operating in what is considered one of the most prolific shale formations outside of the United States. Vista's low-cost production and growing export capacity benefit from rising global energy demand.
VRT: Vertiv Holdings designs and manufactures critical digital infrastructure technology for data centers, communication networks, and industrial applications. The company's products include power management, thermal management, and IT management solutions essential for data center operations. Vertiv is a direct beneficiary of the massive AI-driven data center buildout, with its liquid cooling solutions addressing the heat challenges of GPU-dense AI infrastructure.
VRTX: Vertex Pharmaceuticals is a global biotechnology company focused on developing therapies for cystic fibrosis, pain, kidney disease, and other serious conditions. The company dominates the cystic fibrosis market with its Trikafta franchise, which treats approximately 90% of CF patients. Vertex's pain program, including the non-opioid treatment VX-548, represents a significant pipeline opportunity.
WDC: Western Digital Corporation is a leading data storage company, manufacturing hard disk drives (HDDs) and flash-based solid-state drives (SSDs). The company's storage products serve data centers, enterprise customers, and consumers. With AI training and inference generating massive data storage requirements, Western Digital's enterprise SSD and capacity HDD businesses are positioned for growth.
XYL: Xylem Inc. is a leading global water technology company providing solutions for water and wastewater utilities, industrial customers, and commercial buildings. The company's products include pumps, treatment systems, testing equipment, and smart metering solutions. Xylem's acquisition of Evoqua Water Technologies has created the largest pure-play water technology company, addressing critical global water infrastructure needs.
YOU: Clear Secure Inc. operates CLEAR, a biometric identity verification platform that enables members to use their eyes and fingerprints to verify their identity for faster access at airports, sports venues, and healthcare facilities. The company has over 17 million members and is expanding beyond travel into healthcare verification, age verification, and broader identity platform use cases.
YUMC: Yum China Holdings is the largest restaurant company in China, operating approximately 14,000 restaurants across KFC, Pizza Hut, Taco Bell, Lavazza, and other brands. As the exclusive licensee of Yum! Brands in China, the company serves millions of customers daily through a combination of dine-in, delivery, and digital ordering. Yum China's digital ecosystem and loyalty program drive strong customer engagement.
ZS: Zscaler Inc. is a leading cloud security company that provides a zero trust exchange platform, enabling secure access to applications and data regardless of user location. The company's cloud-native architecture replaces traditional network security appliances, providing faster, more secure connections for the modern hybrid workforce. Zscaler's platform processes over 300 billion daily transactions for over 6,000 customers.
